help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:187  The first line answers the question the timer cannot: it reads the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:188  `run-state.json` written by the last `run-once` pass. Three distinct
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:189  answers, and only the first is a healthy one:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:190  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:191  * last run recent and successful -> exit 0
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:192  * last run FAILED -> exit 1, saying which step failed

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:195    usually leaves a *successful* last run behind, so this overdue check
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:196    is the only thing that catches it.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:319  Initialise a new destination as a *full extra copy* (ADR-013).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:320  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:321  Order is fixed: re-collect from the local sources first (they are the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:322  truth, and rereading them puts no load on an existing destination),
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:323  then copy back only what an existing destination holds and the local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:324  source no longer does, then push the result. The new destination ends
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:325  up with `local ∪ existing destinations`.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:326  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:327  A source destination that cannot be consulted makes the difference set

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:370  Search one destination's archive by session metadata.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:371  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:372  Metadata tier only: this walks snapshot/index/tree objects and never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:373  fetches or decrypts a data blob, which is why it is cheap. On a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:374  three-session fixture the metadata walk read 11,761 bytes against
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:375  1,206,285 bytes of data packs — two orders of magnitude apart. Use
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:376  `--cost` to see what a full-text pass over the current hits *would*
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:377  cost before asking for one; full-text matching is not implemented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:378  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:379  One destination per run, always named: there is no automatic merge
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:380  across destinations, and no default destination to search "everything".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:381  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:382  Exit codes distinguish the three answers, because two of them look the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:383  same and mean opposite things: `0` matched something, `1` read the whole
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:384  destination and nothing matched, `3` could not finish reading it — so
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:385  "nothing matched" is unproven. `2` is a usage error, as elsewhere.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:387  Destination to search. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:421  Open an ephemeral local web view of one destination's session list.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:422  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:423  Binds a short-lived HTTP server on `127.0.0.1` with an OS-assigned port
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:424  (never `0.0.0.0`, never a fixed port), prints the URL, optionally opens
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:425  your browser, and exits when idle or on Ctrl+C. Nothing is installed:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:426  no launchd, no systemd, no background process, no resident daemon.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:427  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:428  THREAT, stated plainly: loopback is NOT a security boundary. Every other
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:429  program running on this machine can connect to `127.0.0.1`, so this is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:430  not "safe because it's local". Access is gated by a random token that is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:431  generated fresh on every launch and appears only in the printed URL —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:432  never in a file, never in a log. Requests without that exact token are
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:433  refused (403), and any method other than GET is refused (405). Treat the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:434  URL as a secret for the lifetime of the process.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:435  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:436  Metadata tier only, same as `search`: machine, first 8 chars of the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:437  session id, shard count, byte length, archive time. Conversation text is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:438  NOT loaded and there is no full-text search; the page says so and prints
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:439  what loading it would cost. Exit codes match `search`: 0 listed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:440  something, 1 read it all and there was nothing, 3 could not finish
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:441  reading (or no key), 2 usage error.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:443  Destination to view. Required unless an explicit `--repo` is given:

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:571  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:572  The stage is an unbounded local full copy; nothing ever shrinks it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:573  This command retires the shard body once every declared destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:574  proves it holds each session. Proof means asking the archive itself —
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:575  never the local cursor — for every session's digest triple (shard
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:576  count / concatenated bytes / concatenated sha256) and matching it
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:577  against the stage. A destination that cannot be consulted is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:578  "unproven" and blocks the reclaim: it is never treated as "does not
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:579  have it". Every declared destination must prove it holds each session,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:580  or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:581  nothing is deleted.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:582  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:583  Default is a dry run that reports what would be reclaimed and deletes

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:585  each machine's retained summaries first, then deletes session by
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:586  session, keeping each session's persistent `shard-seq` counter so the

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:619  overridden by the browser-level "ask where to save each file before
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:620  downloading" preference, which no extension flag can suppress. At up to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:621  200 backfilled conversations a day that is 200 modal dialogs.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:622  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:623  This is one command instead of the five physical actions Native
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:624  Messaging otherwise costs: it renders the host manifest (`name` /
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:625  `description` / the absolute `path` of *this* executable / `type:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:626  stdio` / the pinned extension allowlist) and drops it into each
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:627  installed browser's discovery directory. No elevation: everything is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:628  per-user.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:629  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:630  Every path written, left alone, skipped or removed is printed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:631  absolutely. "No error" is not the same claim as "a file landed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:632  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:633  Idempotent: run it twice and there is exactly one manifest per browser,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:634  byte-identical, exit 0 both times. Exit codes: 0 = at least one manifest
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:635  is in place (or, for `--uninstall`, removal finished), 3 = nothing was
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:636  written because no known browser was found, 2 = usage error (bad host
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:637  name / extension id / relative binary path), 1 = an action failed.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:639  Browser to register with, repeatable. Default: every browser whose
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:640  data directory exists on this machine. Naming one explicitly writes
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:641  it even when that directory is absent.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:644  Discovery root override (macOS default: `~/Library/Application
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:645  Support`). This is what makes the command testable without writing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:646  into a real browser directory.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:649  Which OS path layout to use. Default: this platform.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:669  Windows only: skip the `reg.exe` step and only write the JSON.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:672  Stage the browser-spawned host is allowed to write to. Recorded in
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:673  the config as `[native_host] stage`. The directory must already
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:674  exist and be a directory: the host never creates a stage, and a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:675  stage that appears because a host was pointed at it is a stage
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:676  nothing pushes. The edit preserves the config file's comments and
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:677  everything else in it.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:681  The Native Messaging host process itself.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:682  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:683  Runs the same one-request-one-response loop the browser launch uses:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:684  reads one length-prefixed request frame from stdin, writes one response
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:685  frame to stdout, exits 0. Useful for driving the host by hand before any
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:686  browser is involved. Each process serves exactly one request — the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:687  browser starts one process per message, and the host is built for that.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:688  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:689  Nothing but that one frame may ever reach stdout: Chromium reads stdout
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:690  as a `u32` frame length, so a stray log line is read as a multi-gigabyte
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:691  frame and kills the pipe. Diagnostics go to stderr. A frame that ends
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:692  early (EOF inside the length prefix or the body) is answered with
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:693  silence and a non-zero exit, never with a response.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:694  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:695  `--self-test` prints one line of JSON on stdout and exits 0, unchanged:
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:696  it answers "does the host process start at all?" without needing a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:697  request.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:699  Print one line of JSON describing this host, then exit 0.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:703  Build the activity sidecar index for one machine partition (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:704  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:705  Walks `<stage>/sessions/<machine>/<session>/<bucket>/NNNNNN.jsonl`,
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:706  concatenates each session's shards in global sequence order, and feeds
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:707  every line through the conversation-time extractor to produce one
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:708  `ActivityRow` per session. The rows are written as JSONL to
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:709  `<stage>/meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl` — the file the `overview`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:710  command reads back out of a destination.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:711  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:712  The harness label is inferred from the session directory name: the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:713  canonical archived ids are `<source>.<machine>.<native-id>`, so the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:714  harness is the leading dot-segment (`claude-code.<m>.<uuid>` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:715  `claude-code`); short forms are handled too (`opencode~abc123` ->
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:716  `opencode`, `cursor.d~xxx` -> `cursor`).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:717  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:718  Metadata only: the extraction keeps a timestamp per line and throws the
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:719  line away. Nothing else about a conversation is ever read, kept or
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:720  printed — the report is counts and the output path only.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:721  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:722  Exit codes: `0` = the whole partition was read and the index written;
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:723  `3` = the stage could not be read (or reading was interrupted) — nothing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:724  (complete) was written; `1` = every session was read but the index file
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:725  itself could not be written; `2` = usage error. Same family as
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:726  `collect`/`search`: `3` means "did not finish / never started", `1`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:727  means "finished and then failed".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:729  Stage directory that holds the sealed `sessions/` tree.

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:738  Write this machine's display-name declaration (ADR-018).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:739  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:740  Writes `<stage>/meta/<machine>/machine.json` — a `MachineDeclaration`
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:741  that carries the human display name, the OS and a first-seen time. The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:742  machine partition is resolved exactly like every other command: config
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:743  `machine` first, then the identity file (generated when missing). The
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:744  next `push` archives the whole stage root, so this file rides along.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:745

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:748  `hostname` elsewhere) is used. If neither is available the field is
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:749  written **empty** and the command says so — a name is never invented.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:750  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:751  Exit codes: `0` = the declaration was written; `3` = the machine

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:767  themselves (sold, dead, in a different building). Each file has exactly

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:770

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:774  Stage directory to write the label into (`<stage>/meta/…`).

help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:780  Display-name override for the target.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:784  Draw the machine × harness activity overview of one destination
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:785  (ADR-017).
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:786  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:787  Opens the destination repository, takes each host's newest snapshot
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:788  (the same cross-machine merge as `read --all-machines`), and for every
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:789  snapshot recursively finds the activity index files at
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:790  `meta/<machine>/activity-v1.jsonl`. The paths carry each machine's own
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:791  absolute stage prefix, so they are matched by the trailing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:792  `meta` / `<machine>` / `activity-v1.jsonl` marker — never by a local
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:793  path. The indexes are parsed into overview rows and rendered as a
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:794  machine × harness matrix, a time-unknown tally and a width-adaptive
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:795  heatmap. Prints counts, machine names and time spans only — never
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:796  conversation content.
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:797  
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:798  A machine that has a snapshot but **no** activity index is listed
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:799  explicitly as "index missing" — it never vanishes silently, because a missing
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:800  index is not the same thing as "that machine had no sessions".
help_doc     crates/chat-stasher/src/main.rs:801
